sites.name: Victoria Peak
sites.fact: The highest hill on Hong Kong Island at 552 metres. The Peak Tram has climbed it since 1888.
sites.hint: The wooded mountain behind the towers of Central.

sites.name: International Commerce Centre
sites.fact: At 484 metres, the tallest building in Hong Kong. It was completed in 2010.
sites.hint: The tallest tower on the Kowloon side, on the western waterfront.

sites.name: Star Ferry Pier
sites.fact: The Star Ferry has crossed the harbour between Kowloon and Hong Kong Island since 1888.
sites.hint: At the tip of Kowloon, beside an old clock tower.

sites.name: Bank of China Tower
sites.fact: I. M. Pei's tower of glass triangles, completed in 1990. It was the first building outside the United States to rise above 305 metres.
sites.hint: The sharp-edged tower with white diagonal lines, in Central.

sites.name: Two International Finance Centre
sites.fact: A tower more than 410 metres tall on the Central waterfront, completed in 2003.
sites.hint: The tallest tower on the island side, at the water's edge.

sites.name: Happy Valley Racecourse
sites.fact: Horses have raced in this valley since 1846. Tower blocks now look down on the track.
sites.hint: An oval track ringed by apartment towers, east of Central.

sites.name: Kai Tak
sites.fact: Until 1998 this was Hong Kong's airport, famous for a low turn over the rooftops of Kowloon on the way in. The runway is now a cruise terminal.
sites.hint: The long finger of land pointing into the harbour from east Kowloon.

sites.name: Tsing Ma Bridge
sites.fact: Opened in 1997 with a main span of 1,377 metres, the longest in the world carrying both road and rail.
sites.hint: The big suspension bridge in the north-west, beyond Tsing Yi island.

sites.name: Lion Rock
sites.fact: A 495-metre peak shaped like a crouching lion. It has become a symbol of Hong Kong's spirit.
sites.hint: The rocky summit on the ridge north of Kowloon.

sites.name: Stonecutters Bridge
sites.fact: A cable-stayed bridge over the container port, opened in 2009, with towers 298 metres tall.
sites.hint: The bridge with two tall single towers, by the container terminals.

sites.name: Ocean Park
sites.fact: A marine and amusement park opened in 1977 on the south side of the island, with a cable car between its two halves.
sites.hint: On a headland on the south coast of Hong Kong Island.

sites.name: Sha Tin Racecourse
sites.fact: Opened in 1978 on land reclaimed from the sea. It holds about 85,000 people.
sites.hint: Beside the river in Sha Tin, north of the Kowloon hills.
